More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Jammu and Kashmir High Court makes AIBE mandatory for advocates enrolled since 2009-10
items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently made it mandatory for all advocates enrolled across the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh since 2009-10 to pass the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) to be entitled to practice law. Although the Bar Council of India (BCI) had made AIBE mandatory for law graduates from 2009-10 onwards, the requirement had not been formally implemented for advocates enrolled with the Bar Council of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. The Jammu and Kashmir High Court has now directed its implementation. A notification to this effect was issued by the High Court's Registrar General MK Sharma on October 10, 2026. The notification lays down that law graduates enrolled as advocates with the Bar Council of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, who graduated in the academic year 2009-2010 onwards, must qualify the AIBE if they have not already cleared the examination. Fresh law graduates and advocates enrolled provisionally will be granted an absolute certificate of enrolment only after passing the AIBE and producing the Certificate of Practice (COP) issued by the Bar Council of India within two years. items.title: Kerala lawyers hold symbolic impeachment of CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.summary: Lawyers from across Kerala gathered near the Kerala High Court premises on Tuesday evening to symbolically impeach Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations concerning the functioning and independence of the Election Commission of India. The assembly was organised by the Indian Association of Lawyers (IAL)with representatives from 88 court centres across the State invited to participate. The lawyers assembled in front of the Kerala High Court Advocates Association Golden Jubilee Chamber Complex at 4:30 PM holding banners and the Constitution and demanding Kumar's impeachment. They collectively recited the Preamble and passed a resolution symbolically impeaching Kumar. " The confidence of the people in the neutrality of the Election Commission, strikes at the roots of our democratic system of governance and further resolve that Sri Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioner of India, be and is hereby symbolically impeached, " the resolution stated. items.title: ‘Peaceful protest a democratic right’: Karnataka govt to review police action on protesters
items.summary: The Karnataka government will review the police action against protesters and journalists during an anti-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) demonstration in Bengaluru on Monday, October 12. Chief Minister DK Shivakumar has sought a report on the incident and Home Minister Priyank Kharge has assured that peaceful protests would not be disrupted. Shivakumar said he had taken note of the police action against protesters and members of the media and sought a full report on the circumstances that led to it. “If there has been any unnecessary use of force or excess, accountability will follow,” he said. The Chief Minister reiterated that peaceful protest was a fundamental democratic right. “The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. We cannot demand that right for ourselves in Delhi and deny it to others in Bengaluru. Karnataka must hold itself to the democratic standards that we expect from the rest of the country. items.title: Karnataka sting row: Ex-CM Siddaramaiah moves court against media outlets, platforms
items.summary: Former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has approached the Bengaluru City Civil court seeking to stop 42 media organisations and digital platforms from publishing videos and related material that he says falsely connect him to a controversy involving a woman. The case came up before Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge B Pushpanjali on Monday, October 12. Siddaramaiah’s suit seeks a permanent injunction against the publication or circulation of two videos, along with clips, screenshots, transcripts and reports reproducing their allegations. He has also asked the court to direct platforms to remove the videos or block access to them. The defendants include Kannada and English newspapers, television channels, digital platforms, YouTube LLC, Google India, WhatsApp, Yahoo India and Facebook India. items.title: Telangana: ECI to hold special camps on October 15, 16 to enrol missing voters
items.summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) will organise special camps on October 15 and 16 to help eligible voters missing from the draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to apply for inclusion. The initiative will also focus on first-time voters and young electors seeking registration through Form-6. The camps are part of a one-month initiative to re-include eligible voters omitted from the draft rolls. According to a memorandum issued by the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Booth Level Officers (BLO) and Booth Level Agents (BLA) representing political parties will be present at the camps to assist applicants in the enrolment process. Telangana CEO Sudarshan Reddy has directed District Election Officers (DEO) and Electoral Registration Officers (ERO) to take necessary measures to aid electors. As part of the drive, BLOs have been instructed to identify individuals whose names featured in the electoral rolls before the SIR but were missing from the latest draft lists. items.title: Delhi protests, assaults and detentions: The 18 petitions filed before Supreme Court
items.summary: At least 15 petitions have been filed before the Supreme Court in connection with the October 10 protests and detention of those who were out on streets demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over his handling of special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the functioning of Election Commission of India (ECI). The protests called by various youth bodies and political parties in Delhi had led to large scale detentions and assault of protestors as well as journalists and lawyers on October 10 and October 11. The petitions before the Supreme Court include writ petitions, contempt proceedings, habeas corpus pleas and intervention applications challenging restrictions on public transport, alleged unlawful detentions and police action against lawyers, journalists and protesters. The petitions are listed before a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. items.title: Delhi court sends CJP's Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to judicial custody for 5 days
items.summary: A Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court on Wednesday remanded Cockroach Janta Part (CJP) activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to judicial custody for 5 days. Das, Ranka along with another CJP activist Ajinkya Shinde were detained by the Delhi Police on October 13 after allegedly entering the barricaded Jantar Mantar site by climbing its gates. The CJP activists took the action a day after Jantar Mantar was de-notified as the designated protest site. While Das and Ranka were remanded to judicial custody today, Shinde was released. Notably, the CJP has been protesting alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. This is a developing story.

items.title: L Murugan quits as Minister of State, fuels Cabinet reshuffle speculation
items.summary: Union Minister of State L Murugan on Tuesday, October 13, resigned from the Council of Ministers and sought to relinquish his Rajya Sabha membership, saying he wanted to focus on strengthening the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Tamil Nadu ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. His resignation has fuelled speculation of a Cabinet reshuffle, with several ministerial positions expected to fall vacant. Murugan was the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs in the Narendra Modi-led government. In a post on X, he announced his decision and thanked Prime Minister Modi for the opportunity to serve in the Union government. “From the son of daily wage labourers to serving in the Union Council of Ministers under the leadership of Hon’ble PM Shri Narendra Modi Ji has been the greatest privilege of my life. Now, I wish to return to the grassroots, stand with our karyakartas, and dedicate myself full-time to strengthening the BJP in Tamil Nadu ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections,” he said.
